newsitem.title: USA: Garzarelli says S&P 500 10- to 15-pct overvalued.
newsitem.headline: Garzarelli says S&P 500 10- to 15-pct overvalued.

text.p: Elaine Garzarelli, who heads Garzarelli Capital Management, said the price-to-earning ratio in Standard & Poor 500s suggested that the index was 10- to 15-percent overvalued.
"The p/e ratio suggests the S&P 500s are currently 10 to 15 percent overvalued," Garzarelli said at a roundtable discussion sponsored by Zacks Investment Research.
Garzarelli, who is also a partner with Zacks, added that the 10-year bond yield was three times higher than the current dividend yield on the S&P 500.
"The only time that has happened was prior to the 1987 crash," Garzarelli said.
Garzarelli, who said her market valuation models have a tendency to project market moves early, said she is still looking for the stock market to decline.
"The surprise will hit when earnings are revised down," she said, adding that she is looking for 1996 earnings to be revised down between five and 10 percent on average.

Garzarelli's cash-flow indicators turned her model bearish in July 1996, and led the U.S. stock market strategist to call for a 15- to 20-percent downward correction from the highs set in late spring.

"Although the stock market appears strong, my idea is that since only 50 percent of the market is participating, the trend is weakening," she said, adding that the Dow Jones Transportation Average was one of several indices that remained below their peaks which were set in the spring of 1996. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
